safetyBoundary: This site provides supplementary learning and formative practice. Only the authorised RTO assessment process and a qualified assessor can determine competency.

videos.title: Work Health and Safety (WHS) | Keeping your workplace safe
videos.selectionRationale: A concise farm-context explanation of hazard, risk, risk assessment and the hierarchy of control without teaching a site-specific work procedure.
videos.contentBoundary: Use for concepts only. The current workplace risk process, supervisor direction and local controls govern real work.

thumbnail.alt: Official YouTube thumbnail for “Work Health and Safety (WHS) | Keeping your workplace safe”, about farm work health and safety, hazards, risks and controls.

libraryCard.closeButtonLabel: Close Work Health and Safety (WHS) | Keeping your workplace safe

videos.title: Got a moment?
videos.authorityClass: Australian national work health and safety policy body
videos.selectionRationale: A short worker-voice clip, including a farmer, that supports consultation and respectful safety communication without relying on a workplace-specific form.
videos.contentBoundary: Use to notice communication behaviours, not as a substitute for current NSW duties or the workplace consultation process.

thumbnail.alt: Official YouTube thumbnail for “Got a moment?”, about workers, including a farmer, discussing work health and safety.

videos.title: Come in Clean - Biosecurity Basics
videos.selectionRationale: Clearly visualises soil, seeds and disease moving on clothes, gear, vehicles and farm machinery, matching pathway and inspection reasoning.
videos.contentBoundary: Use to identify pathways and inspection points only. The current property plan controls products, clean-down steps and release decisions.

thumbnail.alt: Official YouTube thumbnail for “Come in Clean - Biosecurity Basics”, about biosecurity contamination carried on footwear, vehicles and equipment.

libraryCard.playButtonLabel: Play Come in Clean - Biosecurity Basics
libraryCard.closeButtonLabel: Close Come in Clean - Biosecurity Basics

videos.title: Farmsafe Australia National Farm Safety Week 2024 -  Safe Livestock Handling 16x9 Final Version
videos.selectionRationale: A short Australian farm-safety clip that supports behaviour, environment, roles and stop-and-reassess thinking around livestock.
videos.contentBoundary: Use for hazard awareness and pre-task reasoning only. Species-specific handling and movement techniques require teacher demonstration and direct supervision.

thumbnail.alt: Official YouTube thumbnail for “Farmsafe Australia National Farm Safety Week 2024 -  Safe Livestock Handling 16x9 Final Version”, about safe livestock handling awareness in an Australian farm setting.

libraryCard.playButtonLabel: Play Farmsafe Australia National Farm Safety Week 2024 -  Safe Livestock Handling 16x9 Final Version
libraryCard.closeButtonLabel: Close Farmsafe Australia National Farm Safety Week 2024 -  Safe Livestock Handling 16x9 Final Version

videos.title: Indicators of Lameness
videos.selectionRationale: Provides visible examples of changed posture and movement that students can describe objectively before escalation.
videos.contentBoundary: Students observe visible changes only; they do not diagnose, score for workplace use or recommend treatment. Current veterinary and workplace advice controls action.

bestSegment.label: Whole clip; focus on visible movement cues, not treatment

thumbnail.alt: Official YouTube thumbnail for “Indicators of Lameness”, about observable posture and movement indicators in dairy cattle.

videos.title: Farm Biosecurity Essentials: Production Practices
videos.authorityClass: Joint Plant Health Australia and Animal Health Australia farm biosecurity programme
videos.selectionRationale: Connects routine observation, feed and water hygiene, storage, livestock care and reporting to preventing spread.
videos.contentBoundary: Use for relationships and early reporting only. It does not authorise diagnosis, treatment, feed decisions or property release.

thumbnail.alt: Official YouTube thumbnail for “Farm Biosecurity Essentials: Production Practices”, about routine farm biosecurity production practices and early observation.

libraryCard.playButtonLabel: Play Farm Biosecurity Essentials: Production Practices
libraryCard.closeButtonLabel: Close Farm Biosecurity Essentials: Production Practices

videos.title: How the National Livestock Identification System (NLIS) works.
videos.authorityClass: Administrator of Australia's red-meat integrity systems
videos.selectionRationale: Explains the national identification and movement-record chain at exactly the conceptual level needed for traceability and record reconciliation.
videos.contentBoundary: Use for system purpose and record relationships. Current species, device, enterprise and regulatory requirements must be checked in authorised sources.

thumbnail.alt: Official YouTube thumbnail for “How the National Livestock Identification System (NLIS) works.”, about the National Livestock Identification System traceability chain.

libraryCard.playButtonLabel: Play How the National Livestock Identification System (NLIS) works.
libraryCard.closeButtonLabel: Close How the National Livestock Identification System (NLIS) works.

videos.title: Ask the Bureau: Why do we have different climates across Australia?
videos.authorityClass: Australian national weather and climate authority
videos.selectionRationale: A student-friendly Bureau explanation of climate zones using long-term temperature and rainfall patterns.
videos.contentBoundary: Use for the weather-versus-climate concept; current local observations, forecasts and warnings govern real decisions.

thumbnail.alt: Official YouTube thumbnail for “Ask the Bureau: Why do we have different climates across Australia?”, about Australian climate zones and long-term temperature and rainfall patterns.

videos.title: Ask the Bureau: How is temperature measured?
videos.authorityClass: Australian national weather and climate authority
videos.selectionRationale: Shows how an authoritative observation is produced and why siting and method matter to data quality.
videos.contentBoundary: Use to judge source and measurement quality; do not infer a current local condition from the clip.

thumbnail.alt: Official YouTube thumbnail for “Ask the Bureau: How is temperature measured?”, about Bureau of Meteorology temperature measurement equipment and siting.

libraryCard.closeButtonLabel: Close Ask the Bureau: How is temperature measured?

videos.title: Understanding synoptic charts
videos.authorityClass: Australian national weather and climate authority
videos.selectionRationale: Directly explains isobars, pressure systems, fronts and troughs on Australian synoptic charts.
videos.contentBoundary: Use to extract evidence, not to guarantee a local outcome. Current forecasts and warnings control real decisions.

thumbnail.alt: Official YouTube thumbnail for “Understanding synoptic charts”, about Bureau of Meteorology synoptic chart features.

videos.authorityClass: Australian national weather and climate authority
videos.selectionRationale: Shows students where to find local warnings, forecasts and observations on the authoritative Bureau site.
videos.contentBoundary: Website layouts can change. Always use the current Bureau warning and the workplace contingency plan for a real decision.

videos.channel: Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions
videos.authorityClass: Western Australian government department using APVMA label guidance
videos.selectionRationale: Introduces the headings and information architecture of an Australian pesticide label without selecting a product or giving an application plan.
videos.contentBoundary: The current registered product label, SDS, chemical register, local procedures and supervisor control every real chemical task.

bestSegment.label: Whole clip; focus on locating information, not application

videos.title: Plant Identification tips
videos.authorityClass: NSW Government regional agriculture and land-management service
videos.selectionRationale: Models careful observation of plant features before consulting an authorised identification source.
videos.contentBoundary: Observation is not confirmed identification. Current NSW weed information and the local supervisor control any response.

thumbnail.alt: Official YouTube thumbnail for “Plant Identification tips”, about observable plant features used before checking a weed identification source.

videos.title: Improving water quality on farm dams
videos.authorityClass: NSW Government regional agriculture and land-management service
videos.selectionRationale: Uses Australian farm examples to show runoff, water quality, vegetation, habitat and measurable improvement as a connected system.
videos.contentBoundary: Use for environmental pathway and evidence reasoning; current property controls and authorised advice govern real earthworks, fencing or water management.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Responsibilities and authority vary by role and workplace; a generic clip could overstate a learner's authority.

visualEquivalent.rationale: A labelled role-and-referral map makes the local authority boundary clearer than video.

moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: A hazard is a source of possible harm; risk reasoning considers consequence, likelihood and changing evidence.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: See hazard and risk separated in a real farm context before applying the distinction to a new scene.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Which part of the example is the hazard, which part is the possible harm, and what evidence would change the risk judgement?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The hazard–risk–condition knowledge check and scene-analysis response.

moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Controls should be compared by how they act on the hazard, with PPE not treated as the first or only response.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Connect the hierarchy of control to the question of what risk remains after a control is chosen.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Which control acts furthest from the person, and what risk could remain after it is applied?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The control-choice check and residual-risk explanation.

moduleCoverage.moduleTitle: Consult, report and learn from incidents
moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Consultation depends on workers raising evidence and others responding so a safety concern can lead to action.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Hear workers, including a farmer, describe how speaking up supports safer work.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: What makes a safety conversation constructive, and what should happen after a concern is raised?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The consultation-pathway decision and report-and-review response.

moduleCoverage.moduleTitle: Roles, instructions and scope of authority
moduleCoverage.rationale: Who directs work and what must be referred are controlled by the local organisation and supervisor brief.

visualEquivalent.rationale: Students can trace authority without importing another workplace's structure.

moduleCoverage.rationale: The learning purpose is constructing and revising a work plan, which is better rehearsed interactively than watched.

visualEquivalent.rationale: A movable plan shows dependencies, priorities and review points directly.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Routine calculations and clear record entries require active worked practice rather than passive demonstration.

visualEquivalent.type: worked fictional record and calculation pair
visualEquivalent.rationale: Students can inspect units, totals and corrections without copying a real workplace form.

moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Respectful two-way communication helps a team surface issues and agree on a next action.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Notice language and listening behaviours that keep a workplace discussion useful.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Which communication behaviour helps the speaker be heard and leads towards a clear next action?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The teamwork feedback scenario and issue-escalation response.

moduleCoverage.moduleTitle: Match task, tractor, terrain and authority
moduleCoverage.rationale: Even high-level tractor videos commonly include machine-specific operating advice. Task, tractor, terrain, conditions and authority must be reasoned from the local brief, SOP and supervisor direction.

visualEquivalent.rationale: A fictional go-stop-refer map keeps the pre-operation decision visible without showing controls or operating technique.

moduleCoverage.rationale: A pre-start can become machine-specific operating instruction; the manufacturer, local SOP and teacher demonstration must control it.

visualEquivalent.rationale: The visual teaches defect reasoning without naming operating steps or settings.

moduleCoverage.moduleTitle: Farm traffic, attachments and exclusion zones
moduleCoverage.rationale: Tractor and attachment footage can become operating instruction or normalise unsafe proximity. Shared-area controls must come from the local plan and supervised demonstration.

visualEquivalent.rationale: A still scene supports blind-spot, people and boundary reasoning without showing machinery in operation.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Usage records and handover fields are workplace-controlled and learned best through a fictional record comparison.

visualEquivalent.rationale: A side-by-side visual exposes missing facts and unresolved defects.

moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Soil, seeds and disease can move between places on people, vehicles, tools and equipment.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Trace multiple contamination carriers through a familiar travel-and-equipment example.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Identify three different carriers that could move soil, seeds or disease between places.
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The biosecurity pathway trace and zone-entry decision.

moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Inspection should target surfaces, recesses and items where contamination may remain hidden.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Notice where contamination can cling before applying an authorised inspection pattern.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Which surfaces or items could conceal contamination and therefore need an authorised inspection?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The equipment inspection evidence check.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Clean-down products, settings, sequence and waste controls are property-specific and procedure-heavy.

visualEquivalent.rationale: The diagram can show where authority is required without inventing a procedure.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Release criteria and escalation paths come from the current property biosecurity plan.

visualEquivalent.rationale: The visual keeps unresolved contamination visible and directs students back to the authorised source.

moduleCoverage.moduleTitle: Read livestock behaviour and the environment
moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Animal behaviour, people, facilities and environmental conditions interact during livestock work.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Look for observable cues that mean a team should pause and reassess rather than push on.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: What change in animal behaviour or the work environment signals that people should pause and reassess?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The behaviour-and-environment observation decision.

moduleCoverage.moduleTitle: Plan roles for a supervised livestock movement
moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Safe supervised movement depends on a shared purpose, roles, route, communication and stop conditions.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Identify planning and communication points without copying a handling technique.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Which role, route or communication point should be agreed before supervised movement starts?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The livestock-movement role-plan scaffold.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Objective observation versus diagnosis is best tested with still evidence that can be revisited carefully.

visualEquivalent.rationale: A still pair lets students separate seen evidence from inference without implying treatment.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Handling records and post-task review require close comparison of factual entries, not a procedural livestock video.

visualEquivalent.type: complete and incomplete fictional handling records
visualEquivalent.rationale: Students can audit traceability and follow-up fields directly.

moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Objective livestock observations describe visible changes in appearance, posture or movement without diagnosing the cause.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Practise separating a visible movement cue from a diagnosis or treatment decision.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Which visible changes in posture or movement can be recorded objectively before a concern is escalated?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The normal/changed indicator comparison and objective field note.

moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Routine observation helps detect change early, while reporting and expert direction control the response.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Connect regular observation with early escalation without asking a learner to diagnose.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Which routine observations could reveal an early change without requiring a learner to diagnose it?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The monitoring-pattern and escalation-pathway decision.

moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Observation, hygiene, separation and reporting work together to reduce the spread of pests and disease.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: See biosecurity as a connected farm system rather than a single cleaning action.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: How do hygiene, separation and reporting work together to limit spread?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The biosecurity-and-authorised-response relationship map.

moduleCoverage.moduleTitle: Treatment records, withholding concepts and follow-up
moduleCoverage.rationale: Treatment, dosage, withholding and follow-up are controlled by veterinary and workplace sources; video risks becoming unsafe instruction.

visualEquivalent.type: authorised-source hierarchy with redacted fictional record
visualEquivalent.rationale: The visual teaches where each detail comes from while withholding operational values.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Species, life-stage and production needs must come from an approved feeding plan; a generic clip could be misleading.

visualEquivalent.rationale: The map names required information without giving a ration or rate.

moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Feed, water and storage hygiene are biosecurity evidence sources, and observable concerns should be held and reported.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Notice how feed and water quality fit inside a broader prevention system.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Which visible feed, water or storage concern should trigger a report-and-hold response?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The feed-quality concern and safe response check.

moduleCoverage.rationale: The purpose is fictional unit and total calculations, best completed as active worked examples.

visualEquivalent.type: fictional calculation cards with unit checks
visualEquivalent.rationale: Students must do and check the maths rather than copy a real ration.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Record review and follow-up information are best judged in a stable fictional ledger.

visualEquivalent.rationale: The visual makes missing quantities, observations and follow-up easy to compare.

moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: An animal identifier links property of birth and recorded movements into a traceability history.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Follow the identifier through the national system before analysing a fictional record chain.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Follow one animal identifier from property of birth through movement records: what makes the chain traceable?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The traceability-chain check and evidence map.

moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: National system requirements and enterprise records have distinct roles in authorised identification work.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Distinguish the national system purpose from details that still require a current local source.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Which parts are fixed by the national system, and which details still require the current enterprise source?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The authorised-source selection decision.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Devices, restraint, marking technique and equipment use require the current enterprise source and direct supervision.

visualEquivalent.rationale: The canvas covers roles, welfare, records and stop conditions without showing technique.

moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Traceability depends on physical identifiers and movement records agreeing across the chain.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Identify the links that must be reconciled before a record can be trusted.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Which identifiers and movement records would need to agree before the traceability record can be trusted?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The missing, duplicated and inconsistent identifier reconciliation exercise.

moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Weather describes short-term conditions; climate describes longer-term patterns such as temperature and rainfall.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Use Australian climate zones to anchor the weather-versus-climate distinction.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: How are climate zones described using long-term temperature and rainfall patterns rather than today's conditions?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The weather/climate classification check and farm-observation response.

moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Comparable weather data depends on the instrument, siting, method and an authoritative observation source.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: See how the Bureau protects the quality of a common measurement.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: What features of the observation site help make temperature measurements comparable?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The instrument/source/data-quality comparison.

moduleCoverage.moduleTitle: Read forecasts, warnings and synoptic patterns
moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Synoptic charts use isobars, pressure systems, fronts and troughs to represent current weather patterns.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Read chart evidence while keeping uncertainty visible.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: What do the spacing and shape of isobars, pressure systems and fronts suggest without guaranteeing a local outcome?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The synoptic-chart evidence extraction and forecast-language check.

moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Current warnings, forecasts and observations must be checked before a weather-affected work-plan decision.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Locate the authoritative evidence needed before documenting a fictional contingency.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Where are current warnings shown, and which details would you record before changing a work plan?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The weather-contingency decision and communication record.

moduleCoverage.moduleTitle: Authority, labels, SDS and the chemical register
moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: A chemical label has defined sections, while the SDS and workplace register answer different questions.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Practise locating information by heading without selecting a product or creating an application instruction.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Which label section answers a product-specific question, and when would the SDS or workplace register still be needed?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The label/SDS/register source-selection check.

moduleCoverage.moduleTitle: Recognise weeds and compare control approaches
moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Plant identification begins with observable features and is confirmed through an authorised source.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: See which features are useful to record before comparing management options.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Which observable plant features should be recorded before an authorised identification source is checked?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The weed-feature record and source-confirmation decision.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Weather limits and off-target controls are product- and time-specific; an operational spray clip could become stale or unsafe.

visualEquivalent.rationale: The visual teaches risk relationships while returning every real limit to the current label and forecast.

moduleCoverage.moduleTitle: Plan, calculate, record and report safely
moduleCoverage.rationale: A real chemical calculation or plan could be mistaken for application instruction.

visualEquivalent.rationale: Abstract quantities preserve calculation practice without producing a usable application rate.

moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Runoff can connect farm work to water quality, soil, habitat and neighbouring areas.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Trace an environmental pathway through a real Australian farm-dam example.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Trace one pathway by which runoff could carry a farm-work impact into water or habitat.
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The environmental hazard–pathway–receptor map.

moduleCoverage.moduleTitle: Protect soil, water, habitat and resources
moduleCoverage.adjacentClaim: Prevention and restoration choices can support water quality, vegetation and habitat together.
moduleCoverage.reasonToWatch: Compare visible changes with the evidence needed to judge whether an improvement worked.
moduleCoverage.watchFor: Which changes shown support both water quality and habitat, and what evidence could confirm improvement?
moduleCoverage.helpsComplete: The soil/water/habitat control comparison.

moduleCoverage.moduleTitle: Measure resource use before improving it
moduleCoverage.rationale: Resource-use improvement depends on comparing local measurements, which is an active data task rather than a video topic.

visualEquivalent.rationale: The visual makes units, baseline and comparison periods explicit.

moduleCoverage.moduleTitle: Report an incident and propose improvement
moduleCoverage.rationale: Immediate response and legal notification are incident- and jurisdiction-specific.

visualEquivalent.rationale: A generic timeline separates immediate authorised action, factual reporting and later review without stating emergency steps.

moduleCoverage.moduleTitle: Fence purpose, specifications and site constraints
moduleCoverage.rationale: Fence dimensions and site constraints belong to the current brief; generic construction footage could conflict with it.

visualEquivalent.type: annotated fictional fencing brief and site plan
visualEquivalent.rationale: The visual keeps specification reading central without demonstrating construction.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Tool, machinery and tensioning demonstrations would cross the supervised-practical boundary.

visualEquivalent.rationale: The matrix links resources to hazards and authority checks without showing use.

moduleCoverage.moduleTitle: Work sequence, communication and quality checks
moduleCoverage.rationale: A fencing sequence is design-, site- and equipment-specific and must come from the approved plan and demonstration.

visualEquivalent.rationale: The diagram teaches planning and quality checks without becoming a build procedure.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Inspection and acceptance criteria are specification-controlled and best assessed from a stable fictional case.

visualEquivalent.type: condition photo map and handover report
visualEquivalent.rationale: Students can distinguish completed work, defects and referral without seeing repair technique.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Electric-fence component videos commonly drift into wiring, earthing or energiser connection instruction.

visualEquivalent.rationale: A labelled relationship map supports concepts while showing no connections or installation steps.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Isolation and live-system work require the approved design, manufacturer instructions and direct supervision.

visualEquivalent.rationale: The visual emphasises exclusion and authority without stating an isolation procedure.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Fault-finding footage can normalise live testing or unsafe trial-and-error.

visualEquivalent.rationale: Students reason from supplied evidence to the next safe referral point without testing a system.

moduleCoverage.rationale: Planning and handover are record skills; a procedural electrical video adds risk without improving the evidence task.

visualEquivalent.rationale: A fictional record keeps unresolved hazards, authority and next action visible.
